text:
incident-bot: [PAGER] P1: HelioHealth (private VPC) - 75% request error rate to model endpoints via private NLB in us-west-2. Auto-alert: NLB 502/503 spike + healthchecks failing. Pager triggered.

alice-oncall: Oncall Alice here. Paging neteng + SRE. Confirming customer impact: HelioHealth reports production traffic failing.

mei-sre: Looking at CloudWatch - NLB target group shows 2/4 healthy, 5xx rate spiking since 00:12 UTC. Backend instances returning 502s. Health check timeout 2s -> intermittent. Any recent infra changes?

raj-neteng: We rolled tightened egress SG for tenant subnets ~00:00 UTC as part of hardening task. That denies outbound to 0.0.0.0/0 except whitelisted. Could be blocking model pool egress. I'm checking rules now.

jenna-support: CS oncall here — customer says they started a high-volume batch at 00:05 UTC and started seeing failures at ~00:11. They're asking for ETA.

alice-oncall: OK. Priority mitigation: revert the SG egress tighten for tenant HelioHealth to previous state (allow outbound 443 to model pool) and scale NAT path. Raj, can you revert and signal when started?

deploy-bot: Action queued: rollback security group rules for sg-0a1b2c3d (HelioHealth tenant). Command: `aws ec2 revoke-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0a1b2c3d --ip-permissions ...` (request id: rb-73a2).

raj-neteng: Rolling rollback now. Also investigating conntrack / NAT port usage on tenant NAT instances — I see high ephemeral port consumption on nat-helio-01.

mei-sre: Seeing established TCP count spike on model-serving hosts and NAT. conntrack_count ~62k on two hosts, near default limits. Healthchecks failing due to ephemeral port exhaustion and backend app returning 502. Recommending: 1) revert SG, 2) scale NAT pool or add SNAT instances, 3) temporary NLB traffic shift to secondary target group.

alice-oncall: Executing steps: SG rollback in progress (raj), Mei please coordinate NLB weight shift. Jenna please notify customer: we are reverting a security rule and shifting traffic to a secondary target group as a canary. ETA 5-10m.

raj-neteng: SG rollback complete — outbound 443 to model pool restored. Confirmed security group now matches previous allow-list.

mei-sre: Initiating canary: modify listener weights to route 20% to secondary target-group b and 80% to primary. Command: `aws elbv2 modify-rule --listener-arn ... --actions '[{"Type":"forward","TargetGroupStickinessConfig":{},"ForwardConfig":{"TargetGroups":[{"TargetGroupArn":"tg-primary","Weight":80},{"TargetGroupArn":"tg-secondary","Weight":20}]}}]'`

alice-oncall: Canary started. Monitoring latency, 5xx rate, and healthchecks.

mei-sre: Canary results after 3m: secondary target group shows 0 errors, primary still experiencing 502s on two hosts. Shifting 100% to secondary now.

deploy-bot: Listener update applied: traffic shifted to tg-secondary (100%).

mei-sre: Post-shift: 5xx rate dropped to baseline within 90s. NAT conntrack still elevated; scaling up NAT instances + increasing conntrack_max on affected hosts as durable fix.

jenna-support: Updated HelioHealth: "We reverted a recent hardening change and moved traffic to a healthy target group. Service is recovering; engineering continuing root cause and fix plan." They asked for rollback details and a postmortem when available.

raj-neteng: Root cause notes for later: combined effect of tightened SG (blocked egresstowards model pool) and NAT ephemeral port exhaustion under burst traffic -> backend healthcheck failures causing NLB to mark targets unhealthy. We'll include SG change timing, conntrack metrics, and the NAT scaling plan in the postmortem.

alice-oncall: Closing pager: service restored to normal and customer notified. Keeping thread open for postmortem actions: schedule RCA, update runbook to check conntrack on tenant NATs after SG changes, and add automated canary shift playbook.

mei-sre: Filing incident ticket and assigning RCA to eng-runtime + neteng. Will attach graphs and backend logs.

alice-oncall: Thanks team. :thumbsup:
